1800 GOT JUNK Pricing in Los Angeles: Complete Guide

If you’re scrolling through Google looking for “junk removal Los Angeles,” you’ve probably already heard the name 1-800-GOT-JUNK? It’s the nation‑wide brand that promises a clean yard, a clutter‑free garage, and a price you can actually understand. In this guide we’ll break down exactly how the company prices its services in the City of Angels, what factors can change the final bill, and how you can lock in the best rate.

How 1-800-GOT-JUNK? Sets Its Prices

Unlike many local hauling crews that charge by the hour, 1-800-GOT-JUNK? uses a simple, transparent model based on the amount of space your junk occupies. Here’s the basic flow:

  • On‑site estimate: A friendly driver arrives, looks at what you need removed, and gives you a written estimate.
  • Flat‑rate quote: The price you see is the price you pay—no hidden fees, no surprise mileage charges.
  • Payment at pickup: You pay when the truck leaves, using cash, credit, or the company’s online portal.

This approach works especially well in a sprawling city like Los Angeles, where traffic and parking can add unexpected costs for traditional hourly crews.

Weight‑Based vs. Volume‑Based Pricing

Most customers wonder whether the cost is tied to weight or volume. The short answer: 1-800-GOT-JUNK? bases its rates on the volume of the load, measured in cubic feet. The driver will fill a set of standard containers (usually a 12‑ft or 18‑ft truck) and calculate the total space used. Because the company’s trucks are already loaded with a mix of items—think old furniture, broken appliances, and construction debris—the weight of each individual piece is less relevant.

That said, extremely heavy items (like a concrete slab) can affect the “load capacity” of the truck, and a driver may adjust the estimate accordingly. For most residential jobs, however, the volume method is the rule of thumb.

Typical Price Ranges in Los Angeles

Los Angeles pricing can fluctuate based on neighborhood, the type of junk, and the time of year. Below is a snapshot of what most homeowners can expect:

  • Small clean‑out (single room, 2‑3 cubic feet): $149 – $219
  • Medium clean‑out (multiple rooms, 4‑6 cubic feet): $219 – $349
  • Large clean‑out (whole house, 7‑10 cubic feet): $349 – $499
  • Extra‑large projects (multiple trucks, >10 cubic feet): $500+ (custom quote)

These figures are averages; your exact price may be higher or lower depending on the items you have. For example, a single old mattress might cost $79, while a pile of broken drywall could push the estimate up a notch.

Special Situations That Influence Cost

  • Hazardous materials: Items like paint cans, chemicals, or asbestos require special handling and incur an additional fee.
  • Heavy equipment: Large appliances (refrigerators, commercial‑grade washers) may add $50‑$100 per item.
  • Parking constraints: If the truck can’t park close to the load, the driver may need to use a hand‑cart, which could add a small surcharge.
  • Seasonal demand: Spring and summer are peak seasons for garage clean‑outs, so prices can be slightly higher during those months.

How to Get the Most Accurate Quote

The best way to lock in a price you’re comfortable with is to schedule a free, no‑obligation estimate. Here’s a quick step‑by‑step:

  1. Visit the 1-800-GOT-JUNK? website or call their local Los Angeles office.
  2. Provide a brief description of the items you want removed (e.g., “old sofa, three boxes of books, garden tools”).
  3. Pick a convenient date and time for the driver’s visit.
  4. When the driver arrives, point out any items that might need extra care (hazardous, heavy, or delicate).
  5. Review the written estimate and, if it looks good, give the green light to start the clean‑out.

Because the estimate is given on the spot, you’ll never be “surprised” by a later bill. And if you decide not to go ahead, there’s no charge for the estimate itself.

FAQ: Your Most Common Pricing Questions Answered

Do I pay for labor?

No. The price you see includes all labor, transportation, and disposal fees. The driver does the heavy lifting, loading, and cleanup—all covered by the flat‑rate quote.

What if I have more junk than expected?

If the driver discovers that the load exceeds the estimated volume, they’ll let you know before loading the extra items. You can either approve an updated price or remove the excess items yourself.

Can I get a discount for repeat customers?

While 1-800-GOT-JUNK? doesn’t advertise a formal “repeat‑customer” discount, they often run seasonal promotions (e.g., “Spring Clean‑Out Sale”) that can be applied to any new booking. Signing up for their email list is a great way to stay in the loop.

Is there a minimum charge?

Yes. The smallest job—typically a single item like an old mattress—starts at around $79. Anything below that threshold is bundled into the “small clean‑out” price range.

Do I need to be present for the pick‑up?

It’s best to be home, but not required. You can give the driver a key or arrange for a neighbor to let the truck in. Just make sure any valuables are secured beforehand.
